item: U-D1 Per-stage cost data published after 2010 that resolves discovery into three separate stages (target-to-hit, hit-to-lead, lead optimisation) with a cost per work-in-process unit
queries_tried: Paul 2010 'How to improve R&D productivity' cost per WIP target-to-hit hit-to-lead lead optimization preclinical phase I cost table | per-stage drug discovery cost target identification hit to lead lead optimization USD million per project | pharmaceutical R&D model cost per WIP by phase 2020 2024 update of Paul model | Sertkaya 2024 nonclinical stage cost breakdown discovery | PhRMA functional R&D spending split pre-human by discovery sub-stage
failure_reason: No source published after 2010 was located that decomposes discovery into three costed stages. Every modern stage-cost source recovered by Agent A (Sertkaya 2024 E-1012, DiMasi 2016 E-1004, ASPE E-1052, PhRMA E-1042) treats all pre-human work as a single line. Agent C independently recorded the same gap as her UNRESOLVED U-1.
alt_sources_tried: (1) Sertkaya et al. 2024 per-stage cost table via Agent A's E-1012 row - nonclinical is one line, 11.8 USD m. (2) PhRMA 2022 functional split via E-1042 - pre-human is one line, 15.9 percent. (3) Wouters 2020 filings-based preclinical share via E-1007 - one line, 12.4 percent median. (4) ASPE per-study cost ranges via E-1052 - clinical phases only. (5) Direct WebFetch of the Nature Reviews Drug Discovery article page and the Rutgers-hosted PDF, plus a stream-decompression text extraction of the PDF, which succeeded and yielded the 2010 table in full.
best_estimate: Discovery cost per WIP unit: target-to-hit 1.0, hit-to-lead 2.5, lead optimisation 10.0 USD million (2008-era dollars)
best_estimate_basis: E-9001, recovered in full from the publisher-hosted PDF text layer and internally consistent with that paper's own published totals (873 out-of-pocket and 1,778 capitalized per launch), which the model reproduces to 0.02 percent [E-9025]. The dating problem is handled by sweeping the single largest cost term, Phase III cost per WIP, across the full modern published range 89.3-245.8 USD million [E-1012][E-1004] in the tornado, where it ranks 12 of 26 with a swing of 6.57 approvals a year.

item: U-D2 Measured utilisation rate (not lead time, not market size) for aseptic fill-finish lines and for ADC bioconjugation suites
queries_tried: sterile injectable fill-finish capacity shortage lines number global 2025 utilization percent | aseptic filling line utilization rate CDMO disclosed capacity | ADC bioconjugation suite utilization booking lead time 2025 2026 | fill finish capacity utilisation percent biologics 2026 | number of aseptic fill finish lines worldwide
failure_reason: No CDMO or industry body publishes a utilisation figure for either sub-area. Every source located reports market size in USD and a CAGR, which is a revenue measure and cannot be converted into a capacity utilisation. Agent G reached exactly the same wall independently and recorded it as UNRESOLVED, stating that L.E.K.'s fill-finish analysis fetched in full discloses no capacity, no utilization, no CAGR, no gap and no lead time.
alt_sources_tried: (1) MarketsandMarkets / GlobeNewswire fill-finish market reports - USD 18.12 bn 2025 growing 9.0 percent CAGR; revenue only, no utilisation. (2) Roots Analysis aseptic fill-finish market report - same limitation. (3) Drug Discovery News sterile fill-finish operations feature - qualitative, notes multi-year expansion lag and format non-interchangeability. (4) Agent G's cmc_capacity.csv rows G-020, G-023, G-101, G-110, G-111 and the derivation records E-6065, E-6066 - these carry G's uniform lead-time-to-utilisation proxy rule rather than a measurement, which G states explicitly.
best_estimate: Aseptic fill-finish baseline utilisation 0.85 (saturation multiple 1.12x); ADC bioconjugation baseline utilisation 0.80 (1.19x now, 1.67x after announced expansion)
best_estimate_basis: E-6066 and E-6065, Agent G's proxy rule applied uniformly across all sub-areas so that the ordering it produces is more trustworthy than any individual value. Both parameters are swept 0.8-2.0x in the tornado; fill-finish ranks 15 of 26 (swing 3.89 approvals) and ADC conjugation does not enter the top 20, so neither is load-bearing on the constraint-migration conclusion. The load-bearing fact for fill-finish is not the multiple but the 2.5-3 year build-and-qualify lag [E-6019], which the steady-state model cannot represent at all and which is listed as limitation 1 in model_assumptions.md section 10.

item: U-D3 Absolute annual capacity of IND-enabling non-human-primate toxicology studies, in studies or animals per year
queries_tried: nonhuman primate supply IND-enabling toxicology studies capacity per year cynomolgus 2025 2026 | number of NHP toxicology studies conducted annually contract research organization | cynomolgus macaque annual import supply United States research 2024 2025 | GLP toxicology study capacity per year CRO non-human primate slots | research monkey supply shortage quantified studies delayed
failure_reason: No source publishes a capacity figure in study-slots or animals per year. Available data are market size in USD, a species-share percentage, a breeding lead time, and one qualitative statement about unfilled requests. The IQ DruSafe industry survey on NHP use in oncology nonclinical packages is behind a ScienceDirect paywall.
alt_sources_tried: (1) Intel Market Research and PW Consulting laboratory NHP market reports - USD 1,500 m in 2025, cynomolgus 79 percent, 4-5 year breeding lag; no capacity. (2) IQ DruSafe survey on NHP use in oncology nonclinical packages (ScienceDirect) - abstract only, paywalled. (3) Labcorp NHP toxicology service page - service description, no capacity. (4) Agent C's E-3050 and E-3051 - US National Primate Research Centers unable to fill up to two-thirds of requests since 2021, and most research primates consumed by IND-enabling toxicology. That is a shortfall ratio for academic centres, not an industry capacity level. (5) Charles River / Inotiv supply-chain commentary via search - acquisition activity, no capacity number.
best_estimate: Baseline utilisation 0.90; capacity growth 2.0 percent per year
best_estimate_basis: Utilisation 0.90 is set at the same level as the tightest measured GMP sub-capacities rather than at the >1.0 implied by a two-thirds unfilled request rate, because E-3050 measures academic-centre requests and not industry throughput, and adopting >1.0 would make the resource binding at baseline against all other evidence that the system is not currently capacity-bound. Growth 2.0 percent/yr is anchored on the 4-5 year cynomolgus breeding lag [E-9009], which is a biological floor on how fast supply can respond. This parameter ranks 4 of 26 in the tornado with a swing of 21.56 approvals a year, so it is genuinely load-bearing and the uncertainty is material; it is swept 0.7-1.5x and the S6b result that NHP toxicology binds first survives across that whole range.

item: U-D4 A published overlap or correlation coefficient between the attrition mass addressed by target validation, preclinical translation, toxicity prediction and training-data quality (B1, B2, B8, B10)
queries_tried: drug development failure cause overlap correlation efficacy toxicity target validation shared attrition | joint effect of improving multiple failure modes drug attrition non-additive | portfolio model overlapping causes of clinical trial failure quantified | clinical trial failure attribution efficacy safety commercial percentages double counting
failure_reason: No study quantifying the overlap between these failure classes exists in anything reached. The published failure-attribution literature assigns each failure to a single primary cause (efficacy 40-50 percent [E-3012], toxicity ~30 percent [E-3045]) and therefore cannot, by construction, measure how much a fix to one would also fix another. Agent C reached the same conclusion and logged the non-additivity as a caveat [E-3097] with a stated band rather than a coefficient.
alt_sources_tried: (1) Agent C's E-3097 derivation record - states the 11-26 percent joint band against a 21 percent naive sum, but gives no coefficient. (2) Harrison 2016 and the four-company 2000-2010 attrition analysis via Agent C's E-3046 - single-cause attribution only. (3) Sun et al. 2022 review of drug failure reasons via E-3012 - single-cause attribution only. (4) Search of the portfolio-modelling literature for a multi-factor attrition model - nothing with a disclosed overlap term.
best_estimate: Overlap coefficient rho = 0.60 in q_joint = q_max + (1 - rho) x sum(other q)
best_estimate_basis: E-9024. rho = 0.60 is calibrated so the model's joint effect (+14.42 percent) lands inside Agent C's stated 11-26 percent band while its naive sum (+20.76 percent) reproduces C's 21 percent. This is calibration to one published band, not measurement, and it is identified in model_assumptions.md section 8 as the least-supported quantitative choice in the model. Mitigation: the report gives the naive and joint numbers side by side in every case rather than only the joint one, so a reader who rejects rho can read the unadjusted figure directly.

item: U-D5 CDER and CBER full-time-equivalent staffing series for every fiscal year 2015-2025, machine-readable
queries_tried: CDER staffing history full time equivalents 2015 2020 2024 FDA employees growth PDUFA | FDA CDER CBER net hiring data by fiscal year table | PDUFA financial report to Congress FTE table FY2020 FY2024 | FDA FY2025 PDUFA performance report staffing | CDER process FTE 2007 2014 2020
failure_reason: Direct WebFetch of the FDA CDER/CBER net hiring data page returned HTTP 401 Unauthorized, as did the FDA financial-report PDFs. Agent E hit the same 401 wall on fda.gov paths and Agent F recorded HTTP 401 on every fda.gov path attempted for the IND receipt series. Two anchor values (FY2007 = 1,809 and FY2014 = 2,487 process FTE) were recovered only from search-result text describing the FY2016 PDUFA Financial Report, so the origin is one hop short of the primary document.
alt_sources_tried: (1) fda.gov CDER/CBER net hiring data page - HTTP 401. (2) fda.gov FY2025 PDUFA Performance Report and Financial Report to Congress PDFs - HTTP 401. (3) congress.gov PDUFA reauthorization hearing witness statement (Marks, Feb 2022) - contains PDUFA VI hiring commitments (230 FTE target, 212 achieved) but not a level series. (4) Agent E's E-4019 - FY2025 end-state levels, CDER 5,044 (net -1,093) and CBER 1,339 (net -224), which is a level for one year and the year-on-year change, not a decade series.
best_estimate: Reviewer capacity growth 4.65 percent per year
best_estimate_basis: E-9006, computed as (2487/1809)^(1/7)-1 from the two recovered anchors, recorded with circular_risk true because the origin is a search-result description of an FDA report rather than the report itself. The parameter is used only as the reviewer-capacity growth rate in scenario S7. Its influence is bounded: reviewer capacity never becomes the binding constraint in any of the ten scenarios (maximum utilisation 0.88), and the tornado sweeps both reviewer resources 0.8-1.5x, ranking them 9th and 11th of 26. The conclusion that regulatory review is not the constraint does not depend on this number.

item: U-D6 Patients enrolled per programme, resolved by modality and by phase
queries_tried: median enrollment per trial phase 1 phase 2 phase 3 number of participants clinicaltrials.gov analysis industry | average number of clinical trials per approved drug program phase 1 2 3 count per NDA | patients enrolled per approval by modality cell therapy gene therapy antibody small molecule | median enrollment cell therapy pivotal trial versus small molecule pivotal trial | number of patients per new drug approval pivotal trials NDA BLA enrolled participants
failure_reason: The only per-approval enrolment measurement recovered is oncology-wide and not decomposed by modality (12,217 participants per FDA approval across 120 drugs, [E-9003]). The per-phase figures available (20-100, 100-300, 300-3,000) are conventional descriptive ranges published without a denominator, a sample or a distribution, not measurements. No source decomposes enrolment per programme by modality.
alt_sources_tried: (1) PMC8132139 oncology enrolment-per-approval study, fetched in full - 12,217 per approval, 158,810 patients across 1,335 trials, 120 drugs, but oncology-only and not modality-resolved. (2) PLOS One 2008-2019 industry phase III recruitment metrics via Agent F's E-5001 to E-5006 - sites per trial, participants per site, recruitment duration, but not participants per programme by modality. (3) FDA drug review process pages - descriptive phase ranges only. (4) Citeline 2025 clinical trials roundup [E-9004] - trial counts, not enrolment. (5) Agent F's NCI-MATCH and screening-ratio records E-5028, E-5066, E-5067 - screening burden per enrolled patient, which is a different quantity.
best_estimate: Uniform across modalities: 60 patients in Phase I, 250 in Phase II, 1,800 in Phase III
best_estimate_basis: E-9008, midpoints of the published descriptive ranges. Cross-check: 78.5 modelled Phase III programme starts per year x 1,800 = 141,000 participants against 289,129 measured industry phase III participants per year [E-5064], i.e. the novel-NME backbone is 49 percent of measured volume, which is consistent with the independently computed 57 percent IND-side share [E-9023]. The direction of the error from assuming uniformity is known and stated in model_assumptions.md section 4: rare-disease and biomarker-selected programmes need fewer patients but harder-to-find ones [E-3027][E-5028], so the model understates the clinical constraint for precision-medicine modalities. The Phase III value is swept 1,000-3,000 in the tornado, ranking 10 of 26 with a swing of 7.43 approvals a year.

item: U-D7 Measured share of shared-resource demand attributable to non-novel-NME work (new indications, formulations, combinations, biosimilars, non-US-only programmes)
queries_tried: FDA CDER number of original NDA BLA submissions received per year 2023 2024 novel applications count | commercial IND submissions breakdown new molecular entity versus supplemental | share of clinical trials for new indications versus new molecular entities | number of active clinical trial sites worldwide growth 2015 2024 investigative sites count trend | industry phase III trials share novel drug versus label expansion
failure_reason: FDA publishes approval counts by category but not submission counts split by NME versus non-NME, and fda.gov submission-statistics paths return HTTP 401 to the available tooling. No registry analysis recovered splits phase III patient volume by whether the programme concerns a new molecular entity.
alt_sources_tried: (1) fda.gov NDA and BLA calendar year approvals page and the CDER Innovation Predictability Access report - approvals by category, not submissions by category. (2) Agent G's E-6031 - 1,139 CDER commercial IND receipts and 716 research INDs for CY2024, total 1,855, undifferentiated. (3) Agent E's E-4024 and E-4025 - 14,870 active INDs 2024 rising to 15,124 in 2025, growth 1.7 percent/yr, undifferentiated. (4) Agent F's E-5006 and E-5064 - 1,156,515 participants in completed industry phase III trials 2016-2019 and 289,129 per year, undifferentiated. (5) Citeline 2025 roundup [E-9004] - 10,503 phase I-III starts, undifferentiated.
best_estimate: Novel-NME backbone is 57 percent of observed commercial IND flow and 49 percent of measured phase III patient volume; the remainder is carried as fixed exogenous background load
best_estimate_basis: E-9023, derived by comparing the model's own calibrated flows against the two observed series: 654 modelled Phase I entries against 1,139 observed commercial INDs [E-6031] gives 57.4 percent, and 141,000 modelled phase III participants against 289,129 measured [E-5064] gives 48.9 percent. That two independently derived shares land within 9 percentage points of each other is the only corroboration available. This parameter ranks 5 of 26 in the tornado with a swing of 19.64 approvals a year, so it is one of the largest single uncertainties in the model and is reported as such rather than buried. The assumption that background load stays constant while NME load rises is optimistic: if AI compresses discovery for label-expansion work too, every capacity binds sooner than the model shows.
